content_voiceover: This more granular table from a 2024 Blood review breaks adult ALL prognostic factors into three tiers: patient-related, disease-related, and treatment-response dynamics. Patient-related factors are age, treated as a continuous variable but especially adverse over 55 to 60, and poor ECOG performance status. Disease-related factors include a high white count, over 30 for B-cell or over 100 for T-cell disease, unfavorable immunophenotypes like pro-B, CD20 positive, early T-cell precursor, and mature T, and the key cytogenetic elements, Philadelphia chromosome positive disease, KMT2A rearrangement, hypodiploidy, and complex karyotype. Ph-like ALL with mutated CRLF2, TP53, or JAK-STAT pathway genes is also increasingly recognized as high risk. The most clinically important section is treatment-response dynamics, because how the leukemia responds trumps static baseline features. Poor prednisone response during the prephase, incomplete blast clearance by day eight to fifteen or persistent bone marrow blasts at end of induction, needing more than one cycle to reach complete remission, and above all, minimal residual disease positivity from end of induction onward, are the unifying factors that predict outcome and guide transplant decisions.
keypoints: Disease-related: high WBC, Ph+, KMT2A rearranged, Ph-like ALL
Treatment-response: poor prednisone response, slow blast clearance
MRD positivity is the key unifying prognostic factor
keypoint_voiceover: Baseline features matter, but response to therapy matters more. Track corticosteroid sensitivity in the prephase, how fast blasts clear by day eight to fifteen, how many cycles it takes to reach remission, and above all, MRD status, since persistent MRD after induction or before transplant is the single strongest predictor of relapse.
